flags: The overview follows the official tourism itinerary from Anacortes to San Juan and then Orcas, reversing the strip’s broad island sequence. The historical park moment is anchored at American Camp; English Camp is a distinct northwest site.

The cache documents designation in April 2009, but not its campaign or the construction history of today’s full road/ferry system. The inter-camp road is historical context, not asserted to be the current byway alignment.

Dropped the published implication that both camps began in 1859: British Marines occupied their camp from 1860. The 20-foot whale-distance claim is cached but omitted to avoid presenting an exceptional encounter as an expected sight.

The published ferry reservation and reduced-frequency notes are supported by the tourism cache; omitted from the requested narrow practical fields, which focus on closures, seasonal roads, tolls and permits. No live schedules were checked.
Lummi practice is kept in the present tense from the cached park article; no tribal source is available.
